test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Refer to the given series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only, and all counting is to be done from left to right).

(Left) 8 3 2 3 8 8 4 7 9 6 2 3 3 8 2 6 6 2 5 6 4 7 9 7 7 6 7 8 (Right)

How many such odd digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by a perfect square and immediately followed by an even digit? (Note: I will be considered as a perfect square.)
solution:
Given series: (Left) 8 3 2 3 8 8 4 7 9 6 2 3 3 8 2 6 6 2 5 6 4 7 9 7 7 6 7 8 (Right)

According to the question, such odd digits which are immediately preceded by a perfect square and is immediately followed by an even digit:

Required condition: Perfect square - Odd digit - Even digit

(Left) 8 3 2 3 8 8 4 7 9 6 2 3 3 8 2 6 6 2 5 6 4 7 9 7 7 6 7 8 (Right)

Thus, there are no such odd digit which are immediately preceded by a perfect square and is immediately followed by an even digit.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.
